capabilities.candidate_interpretation: The modern batch path dispatches invalidation through host_hal; the GV100 candidate row selects the Volta VA callback.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate address, page-size, and membar semantics on GV100 hardware.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: The candidate batches range records, uses max_ranges=8 to choose between recorded-range invalidations and invalidate-all, and dispatches each recorded range through the Volta VA callback. This is not the old capability-bit branch.
capabilities.validation_needed: Check range count, fallback threshold, ordering, and invalidation coverage on hardware.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: R595 selects sysmem mapping page sizes from the active page tree. The candidate's no-argument GV100 MMU factory wraps the Volta 64 KiB mode and clones the Pascal MMU operations before applying Volta PTE/PDE callbacks; this establishes a static candidate path, not successful large-page sysmem mapping.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate exposed page-size masks, CPU-page contiguity, PTE formats, and sysmem mappings on GV100.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: R595 uses runtime prefetch state and dispatches through the arch HAL. The GV100 candidate selects Turing MMU prefetch helpers; the callback closure audit found the same low-level control operation, but the R580 prefetch_supported assertion is absent from this caller.
capabilities.validation_needed: Resolve the removed capability guard and validate prefetch-fault control and delivery on GV100.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: The old capability gate is absent. The candidate policy can choose VID memory for GPFIFO and forwards that location in channel allocation parameters; this source path does not prove RM acceptance.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate GV100 RM allocation, mapping, coherency, and channel execution with GPFIFO in video memory.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: The modern ISR path initializes the fault buffer without the old capability branch. The candidate contains a GV100 fault-buffer HAL row; class and callback presence do not prove RM interrupt or replay behavior.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate RM fault-buffer metadata, interrupts, replay, recovery, and teardown on GV100.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: Modern fault-buffer initialization invokes the non-replayable path unconditionally once replayable setup succeeds. The GV100 table row is present, but entry layout and RM-provided buffer data remain unverified.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate GV100 non-replayable entry sizing, ISR delivery, and error handling on hardware.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: R595 dispatches VA cancellation through host_hal. The candidate GV100 host row selects the Volta cancellation callback; the old capability fallback is no longer represented as a property bit.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate VA targeting, cancellation mode, and synchronization on GV100.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: R580 sets this flag for GV100 and uses it only to reject the legacy system-wide-atomics UVM ioctl policy. The R595 candidate contains neither ioctl definition nor route nor policy helper, so this is a retired UVM policy surface rather than an unmapped modern HAL capability. This says nothing about CUDA C++ atomic-scope support or older user-mode ABI compatibility.
capabilities.validation_needed: Confirm the R595 user-mode ABI does not issue the retired ioctls, and separately validate system-scope atomic correctness on GV100 hardware.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: External sparse mappings call the active MMU HAL. The candidate Volta MMU mode clones Pascal operations and overrides PTE/PDE builders, so its sparse-PTE callback is inherited; the GV100 encoding is not hardware-verified.
capabilities.validation_needed: Validate the inherited sparse PTE encoding and invalid-PTE fault behavior on GV100.

capabilities.candidate_interpretation: The candidate replaces R580's false PLC property with an explicit GV100 rejection of EnabledNoPlc, returning before overlap removal. This is a candidate-specific compatibility guard, not stock R595 behavior.
capabilities.validation_needed: Keep the exact rejection status and ordering under regression tests; validate RM and external-map behavior on a safe GV100 canary.

limitations: Source anchors establish candidate call paths and callback table selections only; they do not prove that the RM accepts the requests or that GV100 behaves correctly at runtime.

The R580 and candidate prefetch MMU control helper bodies are statically identical after C comment/literal masking and whitespace elision; this does not prove register access safety, fault delivery, replay, or suspend/resume behavior on GV100.

The old scoped-atoms flag only gated R580 system-wide-atomics ioctls; the R595 candidate lacks those definitions, routes, and helpers. User-mode ABI compatibility and GV100 atomic correctness remain untested.

The R595 candidate's SYS_NON_COHERENT peer-aperture path is source-compatible with the pinned GV100 PTE/copy-engine encodings, but RM P2P capabilities, actual PCIe atomics, BAR1 mappings, transfers, and mixed-GPU behavior have not been tested on hardware.

The P2P direction audit proves only the open UVM consumer's index usage and finds no RM capability producer definition in the scanned candidate C/H tree; capability-value direction and hardware behavior remain unknown.
The PLC guard is a hybrid-candidate change and is not stock R595 behavior.
No module was loaded and no GPU, UVM, CUDA, P2P, performance, or endurance test was run.

noncoherent_aperture.interpretation: The R595 candidate adds a Volta path that selects SYS_NON_COHERENT for PCIe BAR1 peers when RM says PCIe atomics are unavailable, encodes the GV100 VER2 PTE aperture value, and maps it to Volta copy-engine NONCOHERENT_SYSMEM. R580 exposes the relevant enum and hardware constants but its UVM peer/CE/MMU paths do not select or encode this aperture.
noncoherent_aperture.validation_needed: On a GV100 pair or safe canary, validate RM P2P capability reports in both directions, BAR1 address mapping, CE source/destination transfers, external-map PTEs, PCIe atomic suppression, and numerical integrity under concurrency.

consumer_direction_contract.bar1PcieAtomics_index_0: consumer uses for lower-ID local GPU accessing higher-ID peer
consumer_direction_contract.bar1PcieAtomics_index_1: consumer uses for higher-ID local GPU accessing lower-ID peer
consumer_direction_contract.index_copy_behavior: UVM copies indices 0 and 1 without swapping
consumer_direction_contract.interpretation: Static consumer-side direction only; it does not establish how RM populates the fields or whether hardware honors the reported capability.

p2p_consumer.validation_needed: Inspect the authorized RM producer contract or capture asymmetric [true,false] and [false,true] capability responses on a safe V100-capable canary; verify aperture choice and numeric transfer integrity in both directions.

prefetch_control.candidate_callback_selection: GV100 row directly selects Turing MMU enable/disable callbacks
prefetch_control.interpretation: For the GV100 path, the removed assertion is replaced by explicit modern callback selection and unconditional fault-buffer prefetch enablement. Source establishes this candidate path, not hardware correctness or delivery behavior.
prefetch_control.validation_needed: On a GV100 canary, validate RM-provided prefetch control mapping, enable/disable transitions, prefetch-fault delivery, replay, suspend/resume, and teardown.
